Marina, you expect the slope to be negative - the closer detection=20
probability gets to one, the less size bias, and so the smaller the=20
estimate. Given that your estimate gets larger, that suggests that=20
smaller clusters are more deteectable than larger ones. Actually, that=20
can happen, because the size of clusters far from the line might be=20
underestimated. When this occurs, Distance gives you a warning. In your=20
case, this can't have occurred. So there is a problem with your=20
regrssion in R.

I wonder if you're taking the intercept as your estimate? That would be=20
correct if you were using x has your covariate, as you want to estimate=20
mean recorded cluster size at distance zero. But this corresponds to=20
g(x)=3D1, so you need to use your fitted regression line to estimate mean=
=20
recorded cluster size given g(0)=3D1.

Steve Buckland
